title: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
description: Tall, tender pancakes with a light tang from buttermilk and crisp golden edges. A short rest for the batter is what makes them rise.
notes: Makes about 12 four-inch pancakes. A lumpy batter is correct; stirring until smooth makes pancakes tough and flat. No buttermilk? Stir 2 tablespoons lemon juice or white vinegar into 2 cups minus 2 tablespoons whole milk and let it stand 5 minutes. To hold finished pancakes for a crowd, keep them in a single layer on a rack in a 200°F oven for up to 15 minutes. Cool leftovers completely, then refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze between sheets of parchment for up to 2 months; reheat in a toaster. For blueberry pancakes, scatter berries over each pancake right after pouring rather than stirring them into the batter.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour (250 g), spooned and leveled
unsalted butter, melted and slightly cooled
unsalted butter or neutral oil, for the griddle

instructions: In a large bowl, whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt for about 30 seconds so the leavening is evenly distributed.
In a second bowl, whisk the buttermilk and eggs until no streaks of egg remain, then whisk in the melted butter and vanilla.

Pour the wet ingredients over the dry and fold with a spatula just until no dry flour is visible, about 15 strokes. The batter should be thick and lumpy. Let it rest for 10 minutes without stirring; it will puff slightly.

While the batter rests, heat a griddle or large nonstick skillet over medium heat (350°F on an electric griddle) for 3 to 4 minutes. It is ready when a few drops of water skitter and evaporate within a couple of seconds. Brush lightly with butter or oil and wipe away any excess.

Scoop the batter by 1/4-cupfuls onto the griddle, leaving 2 inches between pancakes. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until bubbles on the surface pop and stay open, the edges look matte, and the undersides are deep golden.

Flip once and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more, until the second side is golden and the centers spring back when pressed lightly. Do not press down on the pancakes. Lower the heat slightly if they brown before the centers set.
Repeat with the remaining batter, greasing the griddle lightly between batches. Serve hot with warm maple syrup.

title: Menemen (Turkish Eggs with Tomatoes and Peppers)
description: Soft, custardy eggs folded into a thick sauce of sweet green peppers and ripe tomatoes, eaten straight from the pan.
notes: Out of season, replace the fresh tomatoes with one 28-oz can of whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand, and simmer a few minutes longer. Aleppo pepper is mild and fruity; substitute 3/4 teaspoon sweet paprika plus 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes. Whether menemen includes onion is a long-running debate in Turkey, so leave it out if you prefer. The eggs are traditionally served softly set. Anyone who is pregnant, older, very young, or immunocompromised should cook the eggs until fully firm with no liquid remaining. Menemen is usually scooped up with bread; bread adds wheat, so use gluten-free bread if needed. Best eaten right away, but leftovers keep refrigerated for 1 day; reheat gently until steaming.

ingredients.name: mild green peppers such as Anaheim or cubanelle, seeded and thinly sliced
ripe tomatoes, halved and grated on the large holes of a box grater, skins discarded

instructions: Heat the olive oil and butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat until the butter foams. Add the onion, green peppers, and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt. Cook, stirring often, for 6 to 8 minutes, until the peppers are soft and the onion is translucent but not browned.
Stir in the Aleppo pepper and oregano and cook for 30 seconds, until the oil turns red and smells fragrant.

Add the grated tomatoes and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt. Simmer over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 8 to 10 minutes, until most of the liquid has cooked off and a spatula dragged through the sauce leaves a trail that fills in slowly.
Reduce the heat to medium-low. Crack the eggs into a bowl, break the yolks with a fork without fully beating them, and pour them evenly over the sauce. Let them sit for 30 seconds.

Draw the spatula through the pan in slow, wide strokes, folding the eggs into the sauce, for 2 to 4 minutes. Stop when the eggs form soft, glossy curds with ribbons of white and yellow still visible. Cook 1 to 2 minutes longer for fully firm eggs.
Remove the pan from the heat right away, since the eggs keep cooking. Sprinkle with the black pepper, feta if using, and parsley, and serve from the skillet.

title: Blueberry-Lemon Overnight Oats
description: Creamy no-cook oats with chia, bright lemon, and plenty of blueberries. Five minutes of stirring at night makes four grab-and-go breakfasts.
equipment: 4 jars or lidded containers (12 to 16 oz each)
notes: The oats need at least 6 hours in the refrigerator, and overnight is best; that chilling time is not included in the prep or cook time. They keep, covered and refrigerated, for up to 4 days and thicken as they sit, so loosen with a splash of milk before eating. Use old-fashioned rolled oats; steel-cut oats stay hard and quick oats turn mushy. For this recipe to be gluten-free, both the oats and the oat milk must be labeled certified gluten-free, and note that a small number of people with celiac disease also react to oats themselves. Any unsweetened plant milk works, but soy milk adds soy and almond milk adds tree nuts. Frozen blueberries can go in straight from the freezer and will tint the oats purple. To eat warm, microwave a portion for 60 to 90 seconds, stirring halfway.

ingredients.name: unsweetened certified gluten-free oat milk, plus more for loosening
lemon, zested (about 2 tsp) and juiced (1 tbsp juice needed)

instructions: In a large bowl, stir together the oats, chia seeds, cinnamon, and salt so the chia is evenly scattered through the oats.

Add the oat milk, maple syrup, vanilla, lemon zest, and 1 tablespoon lemon juice. Stir well for about 30 seconds, scraping the bottom of the bowl, then let stand for 5 minutes and stir again to break up any clumps of chia.
Fold in 1 cup of the blueberries, pressing a few against the side of the bowl so they burst and streak the oats.
Divide the mixture among 4 jars or containers, about 1 1/4 cups each, and seal. Refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight, until the oats are tender and the mixture is thick and spoonable.
Before eating, stir each jar and loosen with 1 to 2 tablespoons more oat milk if it is thicker than you like. Top with the remaining 1/2 cup blueberries and the pumpkin seeds, if using.

title: Ginger Chicken Congee (Jook)
description: Rice simmered slowly with chicken and ginger until it turns into a silky, savory porridge, finished with scallions, tamari, and sesame oil.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven (5 quart or larger)
notes: The ratio here is 1 cup rice to 9 cups liquid, which gives a thick but pourable congee; stir in up to 1 cup more hot water at the end for a looser bowl. Use tamari labeled gluten-free, since regular soy sauce contains wheat, and check that the broth is gluten-free. For a soy-free or sesame-free bowl, leave off the tamari or sesame oil and add an extra pinch of salt. Cooked rice should not sit out: cool leftovers quickly in shallow containers and refrigerate within 1 hour. Keeps for up to 3 days. Congee sets firm when cold, so reheat with a splash of water, stirring, until steaming hot throughout (165°F). Leftover cooked chicken or turkey can replace the thighs; stir it in for the last 10 minutes.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger (2-inch), peeled and cut into thin coins

instructions: Put the rice in a fine-mesh strainer and rinse under cold running water for about 30 seconds, swishing with your hand, until the water runs mostly clear. Drain well.

Combine the rinsed rice, broth, water, chicken thighs, ginger, and salt in a large heavy pot. Bring to a boil over high heat, stirring once or twice so the rice does not stick, and skim off any foam that rises.

Reduce the heat to low so the surface bubbles gently, and partially cover the pot. Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring every 5 to 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and registers at least 165°F in the thickest part. Lift the chicken onto a plate.

Keep simmering the rice, partially covered, for 35 to 40 minutes more, stirring and scraping the bottom of the pot every 5 minutes. The congee is ready when the grains have burst and lost their shape and the porridge is thick, creamy, and falls from the spoon in a slow ribbon. Add hot water 1/2 cup at a time if it becomes too thick or starts to catch.

While the rice finishes, shred the chicken with two forks. Stir it into the congee along with the white pepper and heat for 2 minutes. Remove the ginger coins if you like, then taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
Ladle into bowls. Top each with scallions, 1 teaspoon tamari, 1/2 teaspoon sesame oil, and cilantro if using. Serve hot.

title: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Hash with Baked Eggs
description: Browned sweet potatoes, peppers, kale, and black beans seasoned with smoked paprika and cumin, with eggs baked right in the skillet.
notes: Cut the sweet potatoes into even 1/2-inch cubes so they cook through in the time given; larger pieces will still be firm when the eggs are done. For runny yolks bake 7 to 9 minutes; for fully set yolks bake 11 to 13 minutes. Anyone who is pregnant, older, very young, or immunocompromised should have the eggs cooked until both white and yolk are firm. The skillet handle stays dangerously hot after it leaves the oven, so drape a towel or mitt over it. The hash base (without eggs) can be made up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated; reheat in the skillet until steaming, then add the eggs and bake. For bigger appetites, fit up to 6 eggs in the pan. Most plain canned beans and spices are gluten-free, but check labels if you are cooking for someone with celiac disease.

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes (about 2 medium), peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
red bell pepper, seeded and diced
black beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
lacinato or curly kale, stems removed, leaves chopped (about 1 small bunch)

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the center. Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a 12-inch oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the sweet potatoes and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt, spread into an even layer, cover, and cook for 5 minutes without stirring.
Uncover and continue cooking for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring every 2 minutes, until the sweet potatoes are browned in spots and a knife slides in with only slight resistance.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, the onion, and the bell pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 to 6 minutes, until the onion is soft and translucent.

Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika, and cumin and cook for 30 to 60 seconds, until fragrant. Add the black beans, kale, the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 2 tablespoons water. Stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until the kale has wilted and turned bright green and the sweet potatoes are fully tender.
Take the skillet off the heat. Use the back of a spoon to make 4 wells in the hash and crack an egg into each one. Sprinkle the eggs with the black pepper and a small pinch of salt.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake for 7 to 9 minutes, until the egg whites are opaque and set and the yolks still jiggle slightly, or 11 to 13 minutes for firm yolks.
Carefully remove the skillet with oven mitts. Scatter the scallions over the top and serve with avocado, if using, and lime wedges for squeezing.

title: Avgolemono (Greek Lemon Chicken and Rice Soup)
description: Chicken and rice soup thickened with eggs and brightened with fresh lemon until it is silky and creamy, with no cream involved.
equipment: Dutch oven or large pot (5 quart or larger)
notes: Makes about 10 cups. The key step is tempering: adding hot broth to the eggs slowly, while whisking, warms them gradually so they thicken the soup instead of scrambling. After the eggs go in, never let the soup boil. Heating the finished soup to 160°F cooks the eggs fully. Check that your broth is labeled gluten-free. Cool leftovers and refrigerate within 2 hours; they keep for up to 3 days. The rice continues to absorb liquid, so thin with a little broth or water and reheat gently over low heat, stirring, until steaming hot but not boiling. Freezing is not recommended because the egg-thickened broth can separate. Boneless thighs can replace the breasts; simmer them 5 minutes longer.

ingredients.name: medium carrots, peeled and finely diced

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, celery, and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 6 to 8 minutes, until the vegetables are soft but not browned.

Add the broth, chicken breasts, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer gently for 15 to 18 minutes, until the chicken registers 165°F in the thickest part. Transfer the chicken to a cutting board.

Stir the rice and the remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt into the simmering broth. Cook uncovered over medium-low heat for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice is tender. Meanwhile, shred the chicken with two forks.
In a medium heatproof bowl, whisk the eggs for about 1 minute, until frothy and pale. Whisk in the lemon juice.

Turn the heat under the pot to low and wait until the soup stops bubbling. Whisking the eggs constantly with one hand, slowly ladle in about 2 cups of the hot broth in a thin stream, taking a full minute, until the egg mixture feels warm.

Pour the warmed egg mixture into the pot while stirring, then add the shredded chicken. Cook over low heat, stirring gently, for 3 to 5 minutes, until the soup is opaque, lightly thickened enough to coat a spoon, and reads at least 160°F. Do not let it boil or the eggs will curdle.
Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the black pepper and dill, taste, and add more salt or a squeeze of lemon if needed. Serve right away.

title: Ribollita-Style Tuscan White Bean and Kale Soup
description: A thick, hearty vegetable soup of cannellini beans, dark kale, and tomatoes, made even more substantial with torn stale bread stirred in at the end.
equipment: Dutch oven or large pot (5 quart or larger)
notes: Makes about 10 cups. Ribollita means reboiled, and the soup is traditionally even better the next day once the bread has fully melted into the broth. Use a plain crusty loaf made from flour, water, salt, and yeast or sourdough starter; enriched breads can contain milk or eggs, so check the label to keep this vegan. If your bread is fresh, tear it and dry it in a 300°F oven for 10 minutes first. For a gluten-free version, leave out the bread and mash a second 1/2 cup of beans to thicken, or use a sturdy gluten-free loaf. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours; keeps for up to 4 days and freezes well for 3 months. It thickens considerably when chilled, so add broth or water when reheating and bring to a full simmer.

ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
diced tomatoes (14.5 oz), with their juices
cannellini beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
lacinato kale (about 8 oz), stems removed, leaves cut into ribbons
stale crusty country bread or sourdough, torn into 1-inch pieces (about 4 cups)

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, celery, and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8 to 10 minutes, until the vegetables are soft and just starting to turn golden at the edges.
Add the garlic, red pepper flakes, and tomato paste. Stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes, until the paste darkens to a brick red and begins to stick to the bottom of the pot.

Add the diced tomatoes with their juices, the beans, broth, rosemary sprig, and the remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt, scraping up anything stuck to the pot. Mash about 1/2 cup of the beans against the side of the pot with the spoon to help thicken the soup.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-low, partially cover, and simmer for 20 minutes, until the carrots are completely tender.
Stir in the kale a handful at a time. Simmer uncovered for 10 to 12 minutes, until the kale is dark, silky, and tender with no chewiness in the ribs.

Remove the rosemary sprig. Stir in the torn bread and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until the bread has broken down and the soup is thick enough to mound slightly on a spoon. Add a splash of water if it becomes stiffer than you like.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the black pepper, and let the soup rest for 5 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt. Ladle into bowls and finish each with a generous drizzle of olive oil.

title: West African-Inspired Peanut Stew with Sweet Potatoes and Greens
description: A rich, gently spicy stew of sweet potatoes, chickpeas, and collard greens in a tomato and peanut broth scented with ginger. Contains peanuts.
equipment: Dutch oven or large pot (5 quart or larger)
notes: ALLERGEN: this stew is built on peanut butter and is not safe for anyone with a peanut allergy. Many peanut butters are also made in facilities that handle tree nuts, so check the label if that matters for your table. This is a home-style adaptation in the spirit of the groundnut stews (maafe, nkatenkwan) cooked across West Africa, which more often include chicken, beef, or fish. Use natural peanut butter whose only ingredients are peanuts and salt; sweetened brands will throw off the flavor. If yours is unsalted, expect to add another 1/4 teaspoon salt at the end. For more heat, swap the jalapeño for half a seeded Scotch bonnet. Check that the broth is gluten-free. Serve over steamed rice. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours; keeps for up to 4 days and freezes for 3 months. The stew thickens as it sits, so loosen with water when reheating and bring to a simmer.

ingredients.name: neutral oil such as sunflower or avocado
fresh ginger, peeled and finely grated
diced tomatoes (14.5 oz), with their juices
sweet potatoes (about 2 medium), peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
collard greens (about 8 oz), stems removed, leaves cut into thin ribbons

instructions: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 to 6 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, ginger, jalapeño, and cumin and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant. Add the tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes, until it darkens and coats the onions.

Stir in the diced tomatoes with their juices, the sweet potatoes, broth, and the remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sweet potatoes are just tender when pierced with a knife.
Put the peanut butter in a medium heatproof bowl. Ladle in about 1 cup of the hot broth and whisk until completely smooth and pourable, then stir the mixture back into the pot.

Add the chickpeas and collard greens. Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes and scraping the bottom of the pot since peanut butter can stick and scorch. The stew is ready when the greens are tender and the broth is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Remove from the heat and stir in the lime juice. For a thicker stew, mash a few pieces of sweet potato against the side of the pot. Taste and adjust the salt.
Ladle into bowls, over rice if you like, and top with the chopped peanuts, if using.

title: Classic Beef and Bean Chili
description: A thick, slow-simmered ground beef chili with kidney beans, tomatoes, and a warm blend of chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika.
equipment: Dutch oven or large heavy pot (5 quart or larger)
notes: Makes about 10 cups. Use a mild American-style chili powder blend, not pure ground chile or cayenne; for more heat add 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon cayenne with the spices. Spice blends and broths occasionally contain wheat-based fillers, so check that both are labeled gluten-free. Ground beef is safely cooked at 160°F, which it passes well before the long simmer ends. Chili tastes better the next day. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours (divide into shallow containers so it chills quickly); it keeps for up to 4 days and freezes for 3 months. Reheat to a full simmer. Shredded cheese or sour cream are common toppings but add milk; sliced avocado, cilantro, and lime keep it dairy-free. Ground turkey works in place of beef; cook it to 165°F.

ingredients.name: red bell pepper, seeded and diced
kidney beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the ground beef and 1 teaspoon of the salt. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, breaking the meat into small pieces, until no pink remains and some of the beef is deeply browned. Spoon off all but about 2 tablespoons of the fat.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 to 6 minutes, until softened. Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, and tomato paste. Stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes, until the spices smell toasted and the tomato paste darkens.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and broth and add the remaining 1 teaspoon salt. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release the browned bits, then bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, partially cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the chili has darkened and the flavors have come together.

Stir in the kidney beans. Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chili is thick and a spoon dragged across the bottom of the pot leaves a trail that fills in slowly.
Stir in the vinegar, taste, and adjust the salt. Let the chili rest off the heat for 10 minutes to thicken further, then serve topped with scallions, if using.

title: Dairy-Free Roasted Butternut Squash Soup
description: Squash, onion, apple, and garlic are roasted until caramelized and then blended into a velvety soup that is creamy with no cream, coconut, or nuts.
notes: Makes about 7 cups, enough for 4 main-course bowls or 6 starters. A 3-pound squash gives roughly 2 1/4 pounds (about 8 cups) of cubes; pre-cut squash saves 10 minutes of prep. If the vegetables crowd the pan, divide them between two sheets so they brown rather than steam. Hot soup expands in a countertop blender: fill the jar no more than half full, remove the center cap from the lid, cover the opening with a folded towel, and start on low. Check that the broth is gluten-free. Pumpkin seeds are seeds, not nuts, but buy a brand labeled nut-free if you are cooking for someone with a nut allergy, since cross-contact is common. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours; keeps for up to 4 days and freezes for 3 months. Reheat to a simmer, thinning with water as needed.

ingredients.name: butternut squash (about 3 lb), peeled, seeded, and cut into 1-inch cubes
medium yellow onion, cut into 8 wedges
sweet-tart apple such as Honeycrisp or Gala, peeled, cored, and quartered
extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the center and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment. Pile the squash, onion, apple, and unpeeled garlic on the sheet, toss with the olive oil, 3/4 teaspoon of the salt, and the pepper, and spread everything into a single layer.
Roast for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the squash is completely tender when pierced and browned at the edges and the onion is soft and caramelized.

Squeeze the roasted garlic out of its skins and discard the skins. Scrape the vegetables, garlic, and any pan juices into a large pot. Add the broth, thyme, nutmeg, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 10 minutes so the flavors blend and the vegetables soften further.

Take the pot off the heat and blend with an immersion blender for 1 to 2 minutes, until completely smooth with no flecks of onion. Or blend in batches in a countertop blender, filling it no more than half full and venting the lid.

Return the soup to low heat and stir in the vinegar. If it is thicker than you like, thin it with water 1/4 cup at a time; it should pour slowly from a spoon. Taste and adjust the salt, and heat for 2 to 3 minutes until steaming.
Ladle into bowls and finish with a drizzle of olive oil and the pumpkin seeds, if using.
